verdict_reason: The headline is exact: Roy & Vetterli's effective rank on the RAW matrix reproduces their Sec. 2.3 closed form erank(A_rho)=exp(2H((1+|rho|)/2,(1-|rho|)/2)) to a worst relative error of 6.255e-16 over rho in {0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.99}. The caveat that keeps it off GREEN is an output-loss path I reproduced directly: unembedding.py:83-147 wraps BOTH SVDs in one try, so forcing ONLY the second (centered, auxiliary) safe_svdvals call to raise turns an already-computed, correct unembedding_eff_rank of 2.6004900059896596 on diag(4,2,1) into NaN.
comparable_reason: unembedding_eff_rank is bounded by min(V, d_model) and tracks width directly: 675.38 / 685.97 / 296.10 / 495.48 / 925.62 for distilgpt2 / gpt2 / pythia-70m / pythia-160m / gpt2-medium, Spearman rho +0.894 with d_model and +0.700 with parameter count. unembedding_purity_mean is computed over a tokenizer-dependent category token set (815 GPT-2 ids vs 818 Pythia ids), which the task itself flags with _meta_purity_cross_model_comparable=0.0 and _meta_comparability_note='tokenizer_dependent_category_token_mapping' -- an honest disclosure, and the right one.
normalized_variant: unembedding_eff_rank_norm (produced downstream in normalization.py / aggregate_results.py, not by the task)
github_reason: Roy & Vetterli (EUSIPCO 2007) released no code; the effective rank is a two-line formula. I verified against the paper's own closed form instead (see paper_number) and against an independent numpy SVD. The purity and alignment diagnostics are BLME's own with no released reference, which the task metadata should say explicitly.
paper_reason: Roy & Vetterli 2007, Sec. 2.3: for the 4x4 correlation matrix family A_rho the effective rank is exp(2H((1+|rho|)/2,(1-|rho|)/2)). Closed values 4.000000000000 / 3.650606353593 / 3.079201435678 / 2.328951521694 / 1.487401275304 / 1.064982249509 at rho = 0 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 / 0.99; BLME's effective_rank helper returns the same to relative errors 0 / 0 / 1.442e-16 / 0 / 2.986e-16 / 6.255e-16.
confounds_reason: unembedding_eff_rank is a dimension count with a hard ceiling at min(V, d_model), so it cannot help but track width: rho +0.894 with d_model, +0.738 with n_layers, +0.700 with parameter count over 5 models (296.1 at d=512 rising to 925.6 at d=1024). embedding_alignment_mean (0.654 / 0.667 / 0.501 / 0.393 / 0.742) is rho -1.000 with the vocabulary indicator, which here is just the tied/untied split -- distilgpt2, gpt2 and gpt2-medium are tied, both Pythia models are not -- i.e. it partly re-reads the unembedding_is_tied flag the task already emits.
defects: CODE / OUTPUT LOSS (reproduced): unembedding.py:83-147 shares one try/except across the raw SVD and the auxiliary CENTERED SVD, and line 136 assigns eff_rank=NaN in the handler. Injecting a LinAlgError into ONLY the second safe_svdvals call on diag(4,2,1) changes eff_rank from the correct 2.6004900059896596 to NaN while all 8 other keys survive. This is reachable: the centered branch allocates W.double() -- for a 152k x 5120 head that is 6.2 GB on top of the 3.1 GB float32 copy -- and the handler's own comment says it was written for exactly that OOM. Split the two scopes.

CODE / DIAGNOSTIC: unembedding.py:74-76 infers tying with np.allclose(atol=1e-5), an ABSOLUTE tolerance on a quantity with no scale. Measured: an identity head and a cyclic-permutation head (matrices not equal, row-wise cosine exactly 0.0) report unembedding_is_tied=False at scale 1 and 1e-3 but True at 1e-5 and 1e-13. Derive tying from parameter identity (weight is weight) and keep numerical similarity as a separately named number.

CODE / PRECISION: unembedding.py:188 calls safe_unit_rows on the float32 W_out_np before the purity k-NN. safe_unit_rows is exact at any scale but still normalises in the INPUT precision, so for a head whose rows carry a large common offset the neighbour ranking is unresolvable. I could not reach this on real heads (gpt2 max|W| = 1.79) and record it as a domain limit rather than a shipped error.

CODE / DOMAIN: unembedding.py:224-229 divides the match count by k without checking that k non-self neighbours exist, so a vocabulary with V-1 < k reports a deflated purity (a 4-row identity head with all 4 tokens in one category and k=20 returns 0.2 where the 3 available neighbours give 1.0). Outside the V >> k checkpoint regime.

PROVENANCE: the study paper section still defines the headline as mean-centred while the task (correctly, per Roy & Vetterli) reports the raw value; on pythia-70m the two differ by 296.10 vs 467.52 (+57.9%). The prose and verification_campaign/tasks.json need to follow the code, not the other way round.
fix: Give the centred SVD its own try/except so a failure there leaves unembedding_eff_rank at its correct value and only unembedding_eff_rank_centered becomes NaN. Replace the allclose tying test with an identity test on the parameter objects (or on data_ptr), keeping the numeric similarity under a different key. Emit counts of attempted/succeeded SVDs so a NaN is distinguishable from a value.
